AGENT EVALUATION · TECHNICAL REPORT · NOVEMBER 2026

CardShopBench

Evaluating autonomous agents in a
capital-constrained resale economy

Vedant Bhatter Independent research & engineering
Results & analysisCodeComparison data

Abstract

CardShopBench studies autonomous agents operating simulated trading-card resale businesses under cash constraints, transaction fees, inventory delivery, and settlement delays. A frozen universe of 75 observed Pokémon card pricing references initializes the environment. This report compares eight completed 14-day episodes across GPT, Claude, Qwen, and Gemini using two matched market seeds. Mean simulated equity profit ranges from $109.24 to $119.53, compared with $17.20 for a matched margin-buying control. We publish execution traces, inference costs, action-validity measurements, and a separate 135-episode baseline sensitivity study. The results characterize this simulation under a small exploratory sample; they do not establish real-world profitability or a general model ranking.

MODEL COMPARISON · NOVEMBER 2026

Four models operating a simulated card shop

8 COMPLETED EPISODES

The comparison covers four models with two completed episodes each: seeds 11 and 22, 14 simulated days, six actions/day, $1,000 starting capital, mixed market and base execution, low reasoning requested, 4,096 maximum output tokens, and pinned providers. The research corpus was empty. Business profit is ending simulated equity minus starting capital; API spending is reported separately.

Controls share the same snapshot, seeds, horizon, starting capital, market assumptions, and daily action budget. Control files were checked for equality across model artifacts. Their direct access to public scenario prices differs from the LLM tool interface.

Business outcomes

All four models exceeded the margin control on both seeds. Mean simulated equity profit ranged from $109.24 to $119.53. Claude and Qwen sold all purchased units; GPT and Gemini retained non-cash assets at the horizon.

Action validity

Across two episodes each, GPT and Gemini recorded zero invalid actions, Qwen one, and Claude 13. Invalid actions consume the daily action budget and remain visible in the traces.

Interpretation

Two seeds per model support descriptive comparisons only, not a reliable model ranking or statistical significance claim. Equity includes unsettled proceeds and estimated inventory liquidation. Price paths and buyer demand are synthetic and are not calibrated forecasts of real resale returns.

Protocol and reproducibility

Claude, Qwen, and Gemini use run 45282574457 at commit c92f0f37b529cc49ddd01f5b4ab63c52e6374cb8. GPT uses run 45293031840 at commit 8cad85761469e9d3296d0e28ccf8c6d44cdb76bf, with sequential execution, request pacing, and bounded transport retries. The simulation, system prompt, seeds, and action budgets are matched; transport settings differ. Original requests, responses, configurations, and file hashes are included in the downloads.

The original 135-episode baseline sensitivity study below uses a 30-day horizon and is separate from the matched 14-day controls above. No live marketplace transactions or forum research occurred in the displayed episodes.

Research question

How sensitive is a purchasing policy to execution friction and market shocks when all policies face the same exogenous market events?

Controlled comparison

Each configuration shares its initial capital, card universe, episode length, and five random seeds. Event-keyed randomness prevents tool-call ordering from changing the market path.

Interpretation

Equity includes estimated inventory liquidation. Positive equity returns do not establish realized cash profitability, and the demand model is a simulation assumption rather than a fitted market model.

BENCHMARK DESIGN

Environment and evaluation protocol

The agent chooses its actions. The environment owns the ledger. A persuasive explanation cannot create a sale, erase a fee, or spend money twice.

Every episode uses integer-cent accounting, delivery and settlement delays, a daily action budget, and deterministic market events. Matched seeds expose each strategy to the same opportunities.

◇

Evidence before confidence

Source timestamps and card variants stay attached to observations. Forum claims are research evidence, never transaction ground truth.

⌁

Stress the assumptions

Reprint and hype scenarios test capital discipline. Three execution regimes expose sensitivity to demand and liquidation discounts.

▤

Make failures inspectable

Tool actions, invalid requests, purchases, sales, and settlements are recorded. Checkpoints preserve environment state.

Execution assumptions and limitations

Baseline defaults: 13.25% illustrative selling fee, $4.50 outbound shipping, $1 inbound cost, two-day delivery, two-day settlement, and 12 actions per simulated day. These are configurable assumptions, not verified fees for a specific marketplace.

Daily sale probability is capped at 85% and decreases exponentially with asking price relative to the scenario reference. Conservative/base/optimistic demand multipliers are 0.55/1.0/1.4; inventory liquidation uses 65%/75%/85% of the scenario reference before selling costs. None is calibrated to observed sell-through.

Current references aggregate unspecified card conditions. This release does not benchmark graded-card valuation, low-pop scarcity, negotiation, returns, counterfeit detection, actual local transactions, or historical forecasting. No live model API calls were made for the published baseline results.

Data selection favors 25 higher-priced eligible variants per selected set ($5–$500), so results are not representative of the entire Pokémon market. The universe is frozen; any future historical study must address survivorship and training-data leakage.
